Title: LSJ: Telepathic Counter and bleeds at or below 0

Messages.Author: mboh...@my-dejanews.com
Messages.Body:
Ok, we had a heated discussion in our last session, and the
turn order rules summary isn't 100% clear (about 90%, I think:).

Situation:
Antonio Delgado bleeds with Scouting Mission for 2 bleed.
Dr. Jest reduces bleed to 0.

Does Dr. Jest's player have to decide to block now or not? Can they
wait for an action modifier? Or is it like any other action where the
acting Methuselah can ask for blockers and the reacting Methuselah must
then decide? We are not in disagreement that you can always play a
reaction card after an action modifier (ie deflect or reduce).

How I interpret the rules:
Target Methuselah decide to block or decline. Since 0 bleed, he declines.
Antonio Delgado uses Threats to increase the bleed back to 2.
All the target Methuselah can do is play reaction cards (but still can't
block)

Mike

Antonio's controller can choose to play a modifier. Or he can decline
and wait for the "no block" declaration. After the "no block" declaration,
Antonio's controller can choose to play a modifier (as can the other
Methuselah's), as usual.

> How I interpret the rules:
> Target Methuselah decide to block or decline. Since 0 bleed, he declines.
> Antonio Delgado uses Threats to increase the bleed back to 2.
> All the target Methuselah can do is play reaction cards (but still can't
> block)

You are correct.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Al...@my-dejanews.com wrote:
> > mboh...@my-dejanews.com wrote:
> > > Situation:
> > > Antonio Delgado bleeds with Scouting Mission for 2 bleed.
> > > Dr. Jest reduces bleed to 0.
>

> In the situation [above], once the bleed has been reduced to 0, can I declare

> the a zero bleed is a unsuccesfull action, and as thus I do not have to
> commit to blocking?

No. You may declare the rule "if this bleed resolves for 0 or less, it will
be an unsuccessful bleed", but that doesn't change the fact that the rule
only applies to the final bleed amount.

You will have to declare "I do not block" before the action can be resolved.

If you do so, the acting player again has the option to play modifiers and
you have the option to play reactions.

Once all parties have declined to play any further effects, the action (being
unblocked) is successful and resolves.

If the bleed resolves at zero or less, the bleed is unsuccessful.



or not to block?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Antonio's controller goes first, but can wait until the "no block"
declaration if she chooses.

Full explanation:

The acting player always gets the next opportunity to "do something".

Now that the bleed is zero, it is up to Antonio's controller to choose
whether to "do something" (modify the action) before the next block
attempt or declaration of "no block".

If she chooses not to "do something", then it is up to Dr. Jest's
controller to "do something" (react) before the next block
attempt or declaration of "no block".

If she chooses to do nothing, then it is up to the rest of the players,
clockwise from Antonio's controller, to choose.

If they all choose to do nothing, then it falls to Dr. Jest's controller
to decide whether to make a block attempt or not.

If she chooses "no block", then Antonio's controller has the first
opportunity to "do something" after that declaration.
And so on.

Note that any time anyone decides to "do something", the opportunity to
do the next thing starts again with Antonio's controller.
